title: tenant-prefill allocator + econ-sim CLI and quant-profile wizard
author: Claire Huang
release_notes: Adds tenant-scoped prefill allocator, an offline econ-simulator CLI for replay-based cost/latency estimation, and a guided quantization profile wizard. Safe rollout behind feature flag; includes console preview and operator docs.
description: Summary: Introduce a tenant-scoped PrefillAllocator that derives conservative prefill budgets, microbatch sizes, and transient burst lanes from tenant profile histograms; add econ-sim CLI that replays exported traces to estimate token-cost, median and tail latencies, and effective tokens-per-dollar for candidate defaults; include an interactive quantization profile wizard that generates three suggested qprofiles (safe, balanced, aggressive) with estimated quality delta and fallback rules. Motivation: Global defaults are brittle across tenant traffic shapes and lead to uneven unit economics. By simulating tenant-level outcomes and producing tenant-aware prefill and quant defaults, operators can reduce cost while containing regression risk. What changed: 1) runtime: pkg/prefill implements PrefillAllocator, tenant policy engine, and conservative safety multiplier; 2) cli: cmd/econ-sim provides replay tooling with S3/CSV inputs and outputs JSON/CSV summaries and suggested defaults; 3) tools: tools/quant-wizard generates qprofile artifacts and a small exportable manifest; 4) web: console preview page to review and apply tenant defaults behind feature flag; 5) telemetry: new sim events and metrics to track simulated cost and estimated quality delta; 6) db: migration adds tenant_profile defaults and a backfill job. Rollout: Feature-flagged under tenant_prefill_allocator_v1. Start internal alpha for 10 tenants, enable opt-in in Console, then staged rollout to opt-in customers. Safety: automatic fallback to global defaults if observed quality delta exceeds 3%; CLI and wizard default to conservative profile unless --allow-aggressive is specified. Tests: unit tests for allocator heuristics, integration tests for econ-sim replay, e2e smoke tests for console apply flow. Notes: Offline sim runs on representative traces showed balanced profiles reduce token-cost by ~12% with <1% simulated latency increase; aggressive profiles can approach ~20% saving but require manual review. CI: initial flaky integration test fixed (deterministic sort); final CI passed. Merge: squash-merged to main. Follow-ups: ENG-2499 to add Bayesian estimator for quality delta and additional telemetry dashboards.
